acceptance.given: A disposable same-host protected local metadata fixture uses actual existing schema/store/authentication entrypoints. It contains two independently authenticated accounts with distinct own read states and an account on a different authoritative home, protected local-node facts and centrally authorized notice/projection input data. Trusted Program composition selects the approved restricted local notification audience/read-state capability. Separately prepare an ordinary project/Runner/background-task capability graph and caller-supplied account/home/node/admin fields. Do not assume a notification implementation, service scope or correct account filtering exists.
acceptance.when: Obtain the actual approved local service from protected composition and perform its real audience query/read-state operations as each matching authenticated account/home; mark only that account own notice read and inspect protected rows. Attempt another account/read-state key, wrong/missing/stale home/local-node binding, revoked current identity, forged admin/context or a supplied project/node/port authority. Invoke direct/legacy/default paths and attempt capability acquisition from an ordinary project task or entry-only implicit ordinary-task path. Independently inspect the actual production/project-visible graph so mere DI presence or an interface name cannot be treated as authorization. Do not invent a public notice ingest/product UI or require another package integration.
acceptance.then: Only the approved protected local node service admits current matching account/home notification audience/read-state operations. Its actual query results expose only the caller permitted local audience/read state and a permitted mark-read changes only that authenticated account key. Cross-account/home, missing/currently invalid identity or a forged context/admin/node/port cannot see or mutate another account read state. Ordinary project/Runner/background tasks receive no implicit notification publication, audience or read-state authority merely from their project role/RequestContext/DI presence; they cannot construct or acquire a privileged service through a default/legacy escape. Valid approved local account operations remain usable through the small same-host contract, separate from ordinary project execution and central publication authority. No new issuer, remote transport, inbox/UI or full notification product is introduced.
